gen-dafont-true-north-fs-supreme: Bold and stocky? Not quite: True North is contemporary, with a tall middle band and curves that refuse to close, while Supreme sits beneath it as a crisp sans whose heavy strip of text keeps every letter held open.
gen-dafont-true-north-general-sans: Stocky and unclosed, True North delivers its tall middle band with curves that refuse to shut. General Sans takes over with low-key, flat letterforms and an x-height that fills the line, so the text moves smoothly around every bend.
gen-dafont-true-north-satoshi: Chunky, contemporary, a little stubborn. True North does that with a tall middle band and curves left open, while Satoshi counters with a soaring x-height and strokes cut to a single width.
gen-dafont-true-north-switzer: True North stacks a tall, stocky middle band over curves that refuse to close, with Switzer beneath it. Its wire-like letters carry even visual mass.
gen-dafont-true-north-work-sans: Curves that refuse to close define True North. Work Sans, a plain sans with c tips that never touch and a high mean line, gives it a modern partner.
gen-dafont-visitor-bitter: Visitor brings gaping-mouthed e shapes and short ascenders over big bowls, like wire bent by hand. Bitter, the slab-serif, grounds it with a very large lowercase.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-epunda-slab: Visitor is nostalgic and digital, all gaping e mouths. Epunda Slab adds a dignified serif with tall rounded lowercase forms and a visibly gaping c, so the two feel like relatives from different decades.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-glegoo: Gaping mouths on every e give Visitor its pixel-era charm, with strokes pulled like solder through a nozzle. And Glegoo, with big counters and curves left unclosed, makes a longer passage feel refined and editorial.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-kadwa: Kadwa reads classic and editorial, its open-ended curves and larger x-height keeping text easy going beside Visitor. Its size can stay modest while Visitor's gaping e shapes do the talking.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-scope-one: Retro wire, softly bent. Scope One then steps in as a refined serif whose counters spill into surrounding space, and Visitor's round bowls and gaping e mouths make the two feel delightfully mismatched.
